The denominator is $3-4\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $3+4\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $3+4\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{7}{3-4\text{i}} & =\frac{7}{3-4\text{i}}\cdot \frac{3+4\text{i}}{3+4\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{21+28\text{i}}{9+12\text{i}-12\text{i}-16{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{21+28\text{i}}{9-16(-1)} \\  & =\frac{21+28\text{i}}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{21}{25}+\frac{28}{25}\text{i}=(\frac{21}{25})+(\frac{28}{25})\,\text{i}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
